correctness.rationale: Extend the permutation by fixing 0. Every right translation is either the identity or this permutation; right translations preserve the flag of whether an input equals 0. This gives self-distributivity, as well as idempotence and bijectivity of each right translation. Nonidentity makes 0 intrinsic. A map into the positive elements has trivial target operation, so the homomorphism equations say exactly that it is constant on each positive permutation cycle, with f(0) freely chosen. Composition-idempotence says it fixes its entire image. For a nonempty proposed image T of size s, these requirements are compatible exactly when T is a partial transversal. Then s cycle values are prescribed, r-s cycle values and f(0) are independent choices in T, and there are s^(r-s+1) maps. The top degree of either polynomial is r, including when r=1. Dividing the weighted coefficients by the known factors recovers the elementary symmetric functions; the monic polynomial with those coefficients recovers all lengths, including repeated lengths and fixed points. A bijection fixing 0 is an isomorphism exactly when its positive restriction intertwines the permutations. For (4,4) and (2,6) the ordinary polynomial agrees and the rank-2 coefficients are 32 and 24. The finite verifier and recorded checks were inspected, not executed; the proof covers all sizes and counts maps onto each specified image, not just counts by rank.
residual_risks: Only the passive stratum is counted; the claim excludes the identity permutation and all retractions whose images contain 0.

value.rationale: The passive stratum is intrinsic rather than an arbitrary choice of labelled subsets. Its complete embedded image description and per-image multiplicities give two readily computed complete invariants that separate actual collisions of the ordinary polynomial. This is more than a new proof of the known conjugacy classification: it shows how much the intrinsic retract data sees, with no enumeration of all self-maps.
residual_risks: The result is specific to the one-column family and does not imply reconstruction by retract polynomials for general quandles.
